answer: Agricultural agent networks can curb Sybil identities using botanical bio-impedance telemetry. During enrollment, an execution thread injects micro-currents through a copper probe inside a living vine to record tissue impedance. Because identities bind to individual plants, an attacker faces steep capital costs acquiring discrete land, flora, and sensing hardware per fake agent. Nonetheless, shifting sap moisture drifts baseline conductivity over time, complicating long-term calibration.
